
### running example  {.smaller}


* [based on Abramson, ‘‘The Aloha System---Another alternative for computer comunications’’ (1970)]{.my-small}
<hr class="vspace" />
* suppose we have shared radio with nodes A1, A2, …, A$n$ and B 
<hr class="vspace" />
* A1, A2, … A$n$ are all trying to transmit to B
* takes 1 ms to send message
* and want to collectively send $k$ messages per second 
   * randomly spaced (exponential distribution)


### some probability

* exponential distribution with mean $\lambda$ 
   * our model for when packets sent
   * "memoryless" distribution
   * knowing when last packet sent tells you nothing about next
   * (yes, not realistic)
<hr class="vspace" />
* probability events occur $< K$ time units apart <br> $1-e^{-\lambda K}$

### quiet time to avoid collisions  {.smaller}

![](/multiaccess/texfig/blind-collisions-quiet-time-to-avoid-collisions.figure.svg){fig-alt="for a 1-unit packet, the time period 1 unit before it starts transmitting up until it stops transmitting is marked in red. A 1-unit packet transmitted just after the beginning of the red time will overlap the beginning of the primary packet. A packet transmitted near the end of the red time will overlap the end of the primary packet."}

* to avoid collision with 1 ms packet…
* can't start packet less than 1 ms before
* can't start packet less than 1 ms after
* $\rightarrow$ need 2 ms without other packet starting for no collision


### chance of collisions?(1) 


* to avoid collision when sending 1 ms packet
* need no other packet to be sent in 2ms period around its start time 
<hr class="vspace" />
* with $k$ packets/sec, chance is approx $1-e^{-\frac{2}{1000}k}$


### chance of collision 

![](/multiaccess/texfig/blind-collisions-chance-of-collision.figure.svg)


### retransmissions  {.smaller}


* what's going to happen when node can't send message
* probably it will retransmit it… 
<hr class="vspace" />
* which means real transmission rate will be some $R > k$ 

   * where $k$ is rate messages are generated

* about $[1-e^{-2R\frac{1}{1000}}]$ chance of each message generated
* so $R = k + \left(1-e^{-2R\frac{1}{1000}}\right) \cdot R$
* $R = k + R - Re^{-2R\frac{1}{1000}}$
* $k = Re^{-2R\frac{1}{1000}}$


### retransmissions (plot) 

![](/multiaccess/texfig/blind-collisions-retransmissions-plot.figure.svg){fig-alt="Plot of packet generation rate (k) versus rate with retransmissions (R) from formula on previous page. It forms a half-parabola from the origin to k≈186,R≈500."}


### thinking about result


* sending 500 one ms (packet or retransmission)/second 
   * using about half the capacity!
* representing $\sim$ 186 one ms non-retranmissions/second 
   * $\frac{1}{2e} = 0.186\ldots$
   * getting about 1/6th the capacity
<hr class="vspace" />
* results hold generally
* seems pretty bad for shared channel efficiency!


### some assumptions we made  {.smaller}


* exponential model assumes transmission time of message X doesn't affect transmission time of message Y 
<hr class="vspace" />
* if node A has messages A1, A2 to transmit, it won't start transmitting A2 until after A1 done 

   * means this model is probably pessimistic with only a few transmitters

* assumes nodes won't look at prior other transmissions to decide when to transmit
